collection.name: Name
collection.deleteBody: {{name}} will be removed. It must be empty.

site.name: Name
site.colorHint: Tints the site in the sidebar, its tabs and its explorer, so servers tell apart at a glance.

test.ok: Connected. The server answered with {{count}} entries at the root.
test.trust: This server key is new. Check the fingerprint before trusting it.
test.saveFirst: Save the site to test it.

site.deleteBody: {{name}} and its stored credentials will be removed.
site.charsetHint: Change it only for old servers that show accents wrong; most servers use UTF-8.
site.speedLimitHint: Caps the transfers of this site, on top of the server's own global and per-person limits. Leave blank for none.
site.proxyHint: Tunnels the connection through a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy instead of connecting directly.
site.jumpHint: Tunnels the SSH connection through this server first, as ssh -J does. Leave the host blank to connect directly.
site.anonymousHint: Signs in as anonymous with no secret saved, as public servers expect. An SFTP server is first asked to let it in without authentication.
site.keepPassword: Leave blank to keep the existing password.
site.timezoneHint: The time zone the server lists times in. Most servers use UTC.
site.askHint: No password is saved. It is asked for when connecting and kept only in the server's memory for your session.

encryptions.optional: Use explicit FTP over TLS if available

encryptionHints.optional: If the server does not offer TLS, or someone on the network removes the offer, the password and the files go in clear text without a warning. Prefer requiring TLS.
encryptionHints.explicit: Starts in clear text and upgrades with AUTH TLS before signing in; a server that does not offer TLS is refused. The first time, its certificate is shown for you to confirm.
encryptionHints.implicit: Speaks TLS from the first byte, usually on port 990. The first time, the server's certificate is shown for you to confirm.
encryptionHints.plain: FTP sends the password and the files without encryption. Use TLS if the server offers it.

keyFile.saved: A key is saved. Choose or drop another file to replace it.
keyFile.hint: OpenSSH, PEM, PKCS#8 or PuTTY (.ppk). The file is recognized by its content, not its name.

status.public_key: This is a public key. Choose the private key instead: usually the file with the same name without .pub.
status.passphrase_required: Enter the passphrase of this key.
status.wrong_passphrase: The passphrase does not open this key.

failures.private_key_unreadable: This file is not a key Transferly can read.
failures.secret_too_large: This file is too large to be a key.
failures.unknown: The key could not be checked. Try again.

reasons.key_type: Transferly connects with RSA, ECDSA and Ed25519 keys; this key is of another type.
reasons.ppk_version: Only PuTTY key files of versions 2 and 3 can be read.
reasons.encryption: This key is encrypted in a way Transferly does not read. Save it again with ssh-keygen or PuTTYgen.
reasons.argon2d: This PuTTY key uses Argon2d. Save it again in PuTTYgen with the default, Argon2id.
reasons.cost: This key asks for more work to open than Transferly allows. Save it again with the default settings.

site.remoteDirHint: The folder the site opens in each time it connects. Leave it blank to start at the root.
site.accountHint: Some older FTP servers ask for an account after the password (ACCT). It is kept in the vault like the password.
site.keepAccount: Leave blank to keep the existing account.
site.interactiveHint: No secret is saved. Whatever the server asks when connecting, the password or a one-time code, is asked to you then and never kept.

import.title: Import sites
import.description: Choose the sitemanager.xml of FileZilla or a file exported by Transferly. Nothing is saved until you choose Import.
import.fileHint: FileZilla sitemanager.xml or a Transferly export (.json). The kind is recognized by its content, not its name.
import.filezillaMasterPasswordHint: The same master password you set in FileZilla under Settings → Interface → Passwords. It opens the encrypted site passwords in the file.
import.filezillaMasterPasswordOk: Master password opens the site passwords in this file.
import.filezillaMasterPasswordWrong: This master password does not open the site passwords in the file.
import.passwordsHint: They are stored encrypted in your vault, which must be unlocked. Without this, sites are imported without a password.
import.onConflict: If a site name is taken
import.rename: Keep both, renaming the new one

reasons.key_file_login: Key file logins are not imported
reasons.destination_blocked: Address blocked by the server policy
reasons.host_unresolvable: Host name could not be resolved

import.secretsHint: They are sealed again in your vault, which must be unlocked. Without this, sites are imported without them.

credential.title: Enter the password
credential.description: This site does not save its password. It is kept only in the server's memory for this session, never written anywhere.
credential.target: Site that asks for its password
credential.rememberHint: Otherwise it is forgotten as soon as nothing is connected to the site.
credential.cardTitle: This site asks for its password
credential.cardBody: Its password is not saved. Enter it to connect; it stays only in the server's memory for this session.
credential.refused: The server refused that password. Enter it again.

prompt.title: {{site}} asks
prompt.description: The server needs an answer to let you in. It goes to this connection only and is never saved.
prompt.failed: The answer did not reach the connection. It may have ended.
prompt.expired: The connection stopped waiting for this answer.

export.title: Export sites
export.description: Saves every collection and site of this workspace, with their passwords and keys, in a file encrypted with a password you choose now.
export.hint: At least 12 characters. Transferly does not keep it: without it the file cannot be opened.
export.done: The file was saved as {{name}}. Keep it and its password apart.
